key: Their flesh and their food reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him.
s: After the pilgrims are told to name God over their camels, the verse turns to the offering itself; al-Tabari, on 22:37 to 22:38, reads what reaches Him as their fear of Him in the sacrifice, offered for His sake and as He bade.

evidence.words: لم يصل إلى الله لحوم بدنكم ولا دماؤها، ولكن يناله اتقاؤكم إياه أن اتقيتموه فيها فأردتم بها وجهه، وعملتم فيها بما ندبكم إليه وأمركم به في أمرها وعظمتم بها حرماته
evidence.gloss: The flesh of your sacrificial camels and their blood do not reach God; what reaches Him is your fear of Him, if you feared Him in them and sought His face by them, did with them what He urged and commanded you concerning them, and honoured His sacred things by them.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Hajj 22:37, at 2631). In his one comment on 22:37 to 22:38 al-Tabari opens in his own voice (yaqulu taala dhikruhu): the flesh and blood of the camels do not reach God, what reaches Him is their taqwa, fearing Him in them, seeking His face by them and doing with them what He urged and commanded; he then says the exegetes held the like (Ibrahim, Ibn Zayd). The sentence paraphrases exactly that, and renders taqwa as fear of Him, as he glosses it, not Pickthall’s ‘devotion’. Plain sense: 22:36 tells the hearers to mention the name of Allah over the camels, and 22:37 turns to what of the offering reaches Him; faithful to day.js. Ibn Kathir, al-Qurtubi and the Jalalayn read it compatibly (acceptance of sincere intent). 43 words; entry-check ok.
